QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_57

question.text: What are the margin requirements for hedging positions in ETIRD?

answer.text: Hedging positions are margined upfront under the clearing corporation's risk management framework, with possible portfolio/spread margin effects where applicable
Hedgers are completely exempt from all margin requirements
Hedgers must deposit 100% of contract value as margin
Margins are computed only at the end of the day with no upfront requirement

explanation.text: The Logic: ETIRD positions, including hedges, are subject to upfront initial margin and extreme loss margin. SPAN considers portfolio-wide risk, so genuine spread or offsetting positions can attract reduced margin where the framework allows. Margining happens at the open-position and client/proprietary level. The Trap: No one is exempt from margin. 100% margin would defeat the purpose of futures. The workbook does not give hedgers a blanket concession versus speculators — the benefit comes from portfolio/spread effects in SPAN, not from a hedger label. Note: Margin treatment in ETIRD is risk-based at the portfolio level, not status-based. Spread positions and offsetting exposures may produce lower SPAN margin only where the applicable framework recognises them.
